subject: health
title: Correction and reflection: trusted-adult support
essentialQuestion: How can understanding substance, medication, and risk-reduction skills help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Trusted-adult support can help with safety, transportation, medical care, or ongoing substance concerns; asking for help should focus on protection rather than punishment or shame.
Use observable facts, reliable information, and the appropriate support route; do not infer a person’s health, motives, or character from one detail.
For trusted-adult support, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build a realistic refusal and help-seeking plan for fictional social and household scenarios.
studentTask: Apply the lesson facts to a supplied fictional case about trusted-adult support. Produce a three-part response that identifies the key concept, chooses a safe and feasible action, and explains the choice with two details from the instruction plus an appropriate support route.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in trusted-adult support; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the trusted-adult support task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required. Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model. Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits. Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options. Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media. Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
extensionChallenge: Apply trusted-adult support under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
